## Part A - Creating Vectors and List
```{r}
#Q1
#A. - vector for the worker's age
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29,
         35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49,
         50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51,
         35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41,
         48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

#B. - data points (50)
length(age)

#C. - minimum age (17) and maximum age (61)
min(age)
max(age)

#D. - the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s age
age[c(13:18, 33:35)]

#E. - the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included
age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]

#F. - modified the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0
age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
age

#Q2
#A.
data(rivers)

river_stats <- c(length = length(rivers),
                 sum    = sum(rivers),
                 mean   = mean(rivers),
                 median = median(rivers),
                 var    = var(rivers),
                 sd     = sd(rivers),
                 min    = min(rivers),
                 max    = max(rivers))
river_stats

#B. - the result with all elements in one vector:
#      length         sum        mean      median         var          sd 
#    141.0000  83357.0000    591.1844    425.0000 243908.4086    493.8708 
#         min         max 
#    135.0000   3710.0000

#Q3
#A.
power <- 1:25

name <- c("Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2", "Tiger Woods",
          "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent", "Cast of the Sopranos",
          "Dan Brown", "Bruce Springsteen", "Donald Trump", "Muhammad Ali",
          "Paul McCartney", "George Lucas", "Elton John", "David Letterman",
          "Phil Mickelson", "J.K Rowling", "Bradd Pitt", "Peter Jackson",
          "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Jay Lenon", "Celine Dion", "Kobe Bryant")
name

pay <- c(67, 90, 225, 110, 90, 332, 302, 41, 52, 88, 55, 44, 55,
         40, 233, 34, 40, 47, 75, 25, 39, 45, 32, 40, 31)
pay

#B.
i <- which(name == "J.K Rowling")
power[i] <- 15
pay[i]   <- 90

power[i]
pay[i]
name[i]

#Q4
veg <- list("carrot", "cabbage", "eggplant", "squash", "okra",
            "spinach", "tomato", "onion", "potato", "broccoli")
length(veg)

#A. - added 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list; the results prints 12 elements, with cucumber and radish being the last two elements
veg <- append(veg, list("cucumber", "radish"))
veg

#B. - data points (12)
length(veg)

#C. - added 4 additional vegetables after index 5; the code prints out the four new vegetables after the fifth element
veg <- append(veg, list("pechay", "kangkong", "ampalaya", "beans"), after = 5)
veg

#D. - data points (16)
length(veg)
```
